reason: Part of a whole (pattern 12), the same rule as 'leaf indumentum' and 'inflorescence indumentum' in the 2026-11-23 review. 'Present/absent' is pattern 15. 'Pubescent' belongs on the indumentum or on the petal.

Narrower: the lobes of the last order of division of a dissected leaf or pinna. 'Ultimate' gives the order in the series, which is lost, as with 'ultimate segment apex' in the 2026-11-14 review. '6-12 pairs' is a count (pattern 03). Serrate and acute are qualities of the lobe margin and lobe apex.

target: flower bract (PO_0009034) subtending a pistillate flower (PO_0025599); the whole is named as in pattern 12
reason: In Cyperaceae (Carex) floras the 'female glume' is the pistillate scale, not the grass spikelet glume (PO_0009039). This follows the 2026-11-14 decision for 'pistillate scale'. The qualities (membranous, ovate, acute, 2.5-3.5 mm) fit a Carex scale.

target: orchid labellum (FLOPO_0980978), central upper-surface region (disc) via the surface/region pattern
reason: The same as 'lip disc' (2026-11-14): the central adaxial region of the orchid lip. Sulcate, excavated, papillose, thickened and concave all describe that region.

target: plant organ lamina (PO_0025513) part_of orchid labellum (FLOPO_0980978)
reason: The flat blade of the lip, as decided for the lip lamina on 2026-11-14 (pattern 12). Reflexed, concave, elliptic and oblong are blade qualities.

target: higher order inflorescence axis (PO_0009081) part_of staminate inflorescence (PO_0025601) (pattern 12)
reason: A palm-flora rachilla: the ultimate flower-bearing branch of the inflorescence, mapped to PO_0009081 as for 'rachillae' (2026-11-14). It is not the grass spikelet rachilla PO_0009080. 'Male' goes on the whole, whose PO class exists. 'Up to ca. 60' is a count.

Narrower: a pouch-shaped floral nectary, usually at the base of the corolla or perianth. 'Nectar scale' and 'nectary scale' got the same rule. Only counts are attested ('with 5 nectar pouches'), so the shape is not needed.

target: flower (PO_0009046) with position peripheral (PATO_0002107) in the capitulum (pattern 04/18); ray flower (PO_0025331) only when the flora calls the head radiate
reason: Marginal florets of a head ('8-15', '24-30 par capitule', zygomorphic). PO defines ray flower as pistillate, but peripheral florets can be neuter or bisexual, so the safe rule is flower plus position. This mirrors 'inner floret' (2026-11-14).

Exact for the part. 'Per dm' is a density unit for the count, like 'per cm' (not_a_part) and as in 'secondary veins per side' → secondary leaf vein. The value is a count of prickles per length of the stem.

In fern floras rhizome scales are flat multicellular epidermal outgrowths (paleae). The qualities fit that reading: stiff, linear-lanceolate, entire, acuminate, length/width. 'Stipe scale' got the same rule. Not rhizome scale leaf (PO_0025278), which is a cataphyll; use that class only in seed-plant floras.

Narrower: the thin, often fibrous, ultimate branches of a root ('in turn producing active, thin ... rootlets'). These are lateral roots of a higher order. Fibrous, fleshy, white and thin are root qualities.
Exact: the leaflets of a pinna in a bipinnate leaf ('28-34 pares de folíolos secundários'). 'Secondary pinna' and 'secondary pinnule' were decided the same way. The pair counts are pattern 03.

A character heading in moss floras, not a part. Its statements are about the propagules: present/absent (pattern 15), plus multicellular, green, simple and length, which are qualities of gemmae or other propagules. Map the heading to the existing propagule class; when the flora names gemmae, use gemma (PO_0025614).

Narrower: a stem in the young state. 'Young' is already a bearer_quality in flora_context_words.tsv, so the compound only needs splitting, like 'male spikelet' and 'young growth'. 'Glabrescent' carries the change with age.

Narrower: the tube above an inferior ovary that bears the perianth and stamens, e.g. the floral tube of Onagraceae. This matches PO's hypanthium definition ('often above the top of the ovary'). Cylindric, crateriform and length are tube qualities.

target: higher order inflorescence axis (PO_0009081) part_of pistillate inflorescence (PO_0025598) (pattern 12)
reason: The pistillate counterpart of 'male inflorescence rachilla': palm rachillae on a pistillate inflorescence. PO lists 'female inflorescence' as a synonym of PO_0025598.

Exact: Spanish 'filopodio' is the phyllopodium. In Polypodiaceae and grammitid ferns it is the short projection of the rhizome to which the stipe articulates. 'Articulated', 'conspicuous', 'absent' and '0.5-2 mm' fit that reading. The grounding failed on the f/ph spelling.

The midrib of the moss perichaetial leaf. 'Perichaetial leaf' maps to PO_0030030 (2026-11-14), and costa is an existing PO class with phyllid synonyms. Excurrent, discontinuous and absent-at-base are costa qualities.

target: sepal (PO_0009031), abaxial median ridge (midvein region); not keel (PO_0025327), which is the legume petal structure
reason: The keel of a sepal is its raised dorsal midrib ridge, e.g. in Caryophyllaceae or Polygala. That is a region of the sepal, not PO's keel, which is the two fused lower petals of a papilionaceous corolla. Alate, scarious, lacerate and ciliate describe the ridge. The '3-6 mm' length is probably the sepal's. Earlier reviews rejected bare 'abaxial/lateral keel' because no organ was named; here the organ is named.
In Carex, 'utricle' is the perigynium; 'utricle beak' was decided the same way with the apex. Cuneate, attenuate, contracted, stipitate and narrowed are base qualities.

An apex region of an existing organ (pattern 12), as decided for other organ apices. Acute, rounded, obtuse and emarginate are apex shapes. If the flora means the lobe tips, use the apex of calyx lobe (FLOPO_0986005).

The veins of the calyx. PO's venation classes cover leaves only, so the vein class is used with the calyx as the whole. 'Prominent' and 'elongated' are vein qualities. 'Undulate/wavy' veins (venation pattern) stay on the same bearer.

target: vascular leaf (PO_0009025) with the dorsal (median) position in an anisophyllous shoot (pattern 18, position of the bearer)
reason: Probably Selaginella, whose dimorphic microphylls form dorsal (median) and ventral (lateral) ranks ('Ventral and dorsal leaves symmetric'). This is a position of the leaf on the shoot, not a new structure, as 'dorsal sepal' and 'inner sepal' were handled. Leafy liverworts use 'underleaf' instead, which is mapped already.

Exact: where floras separate an outer ligule (FLOPO_0986089), as in bamboos and some Cyperaceae, the inner ligule is the ligule proper on the adaxial sheath-blade junction. Membranous, ciliolate, truncate and 1-3 mm fit that reading.

The space between ribs, with no organ named: it could be on the calyx (e.g. Plumbaginaceae, 'membranous hyaline intervals'), a mericarp (between ridges) or a pappus. The record's context is needed. A bare 'interval' must not become a bearer.

Narrower: the larger members of an unequal androecium ('larger stamens 2-4'). The count goes on stamen (pattern 03). The size difference of the set is the existing value unequal (FLOPO_0991101), not a new class.

target: mericarp (PO_0020075) with quality winged (PATO_0104354); wing counts and widths go on the fruit wing class if the one proposed for 'samara wing' (2026-11-23) is added
reason: The wings of an Apiaceae- or Malpighiaceae-type mericarp. Like 'valve wing' and 'perigynium wing', presence becomes 'winged' on the existing organ. Counts ('alas laterales 2') and widths need a wing bearer, which is the pending generic fruit wing class, so no second class is proposed here.
A count container ('Leaves 3-6 per culm'), like 'per fertile culm' and 'per node'. The leaf is the bearer; the culm (stem PO_0009047) is only the whole.
A count container ('ovules 2-3 per placenta'), like 'per valve' and 'per lumen'. The bearer is the ovule (PO_0020003); placenta (PO_0025078) is the whole.

Narrower than plain 'sporangiophore' (→ sporophyll, 2026-11-14): in cycad (Zamia) floras the pollen sporangiophores are the peltate, truncate, cuneiform scales of the pollen cone that bear microsporangia, i.e. microsporophylls.
